title: Bouncing ball

narration.transcript: A big green gym ball bounces on the floor a few times. The ball is about seventy-five centimetres across.

caveats: ball moves partly toward and over the low camera so apparent size changes with distance, not just height
ball is cropped out of the top of the frame at the top of bounces
ball is blurred and out of focus when very close to the lens
mirror behind shows a second identical green ball that could confuse tracking - track the real foreground ball

reference.basis: narrator said the ball is about seventy-five centimetres across

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, on-screen text or narration mentions slow motion or frame rate; bounce timing looks real-time

stated_facts.said: The ball is about seventy-five centimetres across.

observation.what_happens: A large green ball falls and bounces on a wooden gym floor in front of a low floor-level camera. The free bouncing starts while it is already airborne and continues with several floor impacts until the clip ends.

calibration.note: green ball = 0.75 m (narrator said the ball is about seventy-five centimetres across) spans 89 ± 1.1 px in SAM's mask (83 frames)

given: scale: green ball = 0.75 m (narrator said the ball is about seventy-five centimetres across) spans 89 ± 1.1 px in SAM's mask (83 frames), known to ±10% (its size ±10%, its length in pixels ±1.2%)
diameter = 0.75 m (“The ball is about seventy-five centimetres across.”)
reasoning: The track is a straight near-vertical line: s mirrors -y, rising to an apex then falling ~1.4 m to a floor impact and rebounding lower, classic inelastic bounce under Earth gravity. For a 0.75 m ball in air drag may shape the fast fall, so we compete no-drag vs linear vs quadratic drag, all with a restitution bounce event.

caveats: Ball size known only to about ten percent, so heights shift with scale.
Low floor-level camera adds perspective distortion near the floor.
Bounce impacts are brief so contact timing is uncertain.
critique.finding: The ball slides along its track with steady acceleration of {a} and never bounces. It only partly captures the motion, missing the floor impacts completely.
critique.headline: Ball rolls without bouncing, missing the real hops.
critique.revision_idea: Add a floor bounce with restitution that reverses velocity at impact. The misses swing far outside noise in repeating arches timed to impacts, which a smooth acceleration cannot follow.
critique.why_it_won: It stays on one smooth track without forcing bounces at the wrong floor height that drag the bounce laws away.
